title: Bangkok - Creative Districts and Old Buildings
speaker: VICE Asia
description: See how artists and businesses reuse old spaces instead of flattening local character.
summary: This VICE Asia short follows Bangkok creatives who work with older buildings, local streets, and neighborhood memory. The video gives students a concrete way to discuss whether development should always mean new construction. Students can identify the speakers' reasons for preserving local character, compare creative districts with shopping malls, and decide what makes a neighborhood feel alive.

title: Bangkok - The City's Changing Food Identity
speaker: Curious Thing Films
description: Use street food to discuss pride, regulation, tourism, and daily convenience.
summary: This short documentary asks how Bangkok's food identity is changing as street food becomes both a local habit and an international image. It raises questions about regulation, embarrassment, pride, convenience, and tourism. Students can compare local food scenes, decide what should be protected, and practice explaining why a dish or eating place matters beyond taste.

title: Why Tokyo's Metro Is Profitable
speaker: The Wall Street Journal
description: Compare Tokyo and New York to see how connections, land use, and operations shape a railway.
summary: This Wall Street Journal comparison asks why Tokyo's metro can operate profitably while New York's subway requires significant public support. It examines Tokyo's interconnected commuter and subway lines, high ridership, convenient payment cards, frequent service, and the relationship between railway companies and development around stations. Students can identify cause-and-effect claims, compare two transport systems, and debate whether public transit should be judged mainly as a business or as an essential public service.

title: Japan's Ever-Evolving Vending Machines
speaker: CNN Business
description: See why millions of machines fit Japan’s labor market, public spaces, and daily routines.
summary: CNN Business explores why vending machines are so common in Japan and how manufacturers keep changing them. The report connects machines with round-the-clock convenience, limited staffing needs, reliable public spaces, and the ability to sell hot and cold products in compact locations. It also looks at factory production and new machine designs. Students can explain why a technology fits a particular society, evaluate convenience against labor and waste concerns, and propose a vending-machine service for their own city.

title: Tokyo Time Scape: How the City Rebuilt Itself
speaker: Tokyo Metropolitan Government
description: Trace Tokyo from Edo’s waterways through railways, reconstruction, and modern urban planning.
summary: This official Tokyo Metropolitan Government short traces the city's development from Edo to the modern metropolis. It explains the importance of roads and waterways, reconstruction after fires and disasters, the arrival of railways and Western technologies, postwar growth, Olympic-era infrastructure, and later urban-renewal plans. Students can build a timeline, identify how problems led to planning changes, and discuss whether a city's identity survives repeated rebuilding.

title: Seoul - How the Subway Carries the City
speaker: Seoul Metropolitan Rapid Transit Corp.
description: Use an official transit film to discuss reliability, scale, and public-service language.
summary: This official corporate film introduces Seoul subway lines, stations, service goals, and the idea of transport as a public promise. Students can compare the language of public-service branding with the practical needs of commuters, then explain what makes a subway system feel reliable, safe, and easy to use.

title: Seoul - Gyeongbokgung Palace in a Modern Capital
speaker: Viator
description: Visit a palace site and notice color, ceremony, architecture, and public memory.
summary: This short palace visit gives students a quick visual and listening entry point into Gyeongbokgung. The clip works well for lower-level classes because the language is simple and concrete. Students can describe what they see, compare palace behavior with shopping-street behavior, and discuss why historic places remain important in a fast modern city.

title: Seoul - Korea in Five Minutes
speaker: History on Maps
description: Build a timeline from early kingdoms to division, rebuilding, and modern South Korea.
summary: This fast history overview gives context for Seoul as a capital shaped by kingdoms, invasion, colonization, war, division, industrialization, and global influence. Students can practice timeline language, separate major events from details, and discuss how a capital city carries national memory.

title: Singapore - Why the City Feels So Designed
speaker: Kleos
description: Connect public housing, transit, land scarcity, and planning into one city system.
summary: This explainer focuses on Singapore's design logic: limited land, public housing, transport, green space, and government planning. Students can identify linked causes and effects, compare planned and less-planned cities, and debate whether strong planning creates comfort, control, or both.

title: Singapore - Why Hawker Culture Matters
speaker: The Straits Times
description: Hear Singaporeans explain why hawker centres are food, memory, and community.
summary: This Straits Times short uses hawker dishes and public voices to explain why hawker culture matters in Singapore. Students can practice food vocabulary, identify reasons people value shared eating places, and compare hawker centres with food courts, markets, cafeterias, or street-food areas in other cities.

title: Singapore - Changi Airport's Lifestyle Hub
speaker: Business Insider
description: Look at Jewel Changi and ask why an airport would become a public destination.
summary: This Business Insider video explains Jewel Changi as a lifestyle hub with gardens, retail, an indoor waterfall, and airport connectivity. Students can discuss how design changes the stress of travel, whether airports should become destinations, and what services tired passengers actually need.

title: Paris - Cafe Culture and Public Life
speaker: Rick Steves' Europe
description: Use a short travel bite to discuss conversation, time, and people-watching.
summary: This quick cafe segment gives students a simple, concrete entry into Paris public life. It works well for speaking practice because students can describe atmosphere, compare cafe routines, and decide whether a cafe is mainly a business, a social space, a workplace, or a place to slow down.

title: Paris - The Louvre in 800 Years
speaker: Musee du Louvre
description: Trace the Louvre from medieval fortress to royal palace to public museum.
summary: This official Louvre video shows how the building changed from fortress to palace to museum. Students can track how architecture reflects political power, public access, and cultural memory. The short length also makes it useful before a discussion on who museums are for.

title: London - Sightseeing in Simple English
speaker: Loescher Editore video
description: Use an A1-A2 city tour to practice landmarks, numbers, and short descriptions.
summary: This simple London sightseeing video is useful for lower-level classes because the language is clear, short, and landmark-based. Students can practice describing what they see, asking basic travel questions, and building a simple route through the city.

title: London - How the Underground Works
speaker: National Geographic
description: Look inside the Tube as an engineering system, not only a famous map.
summary: This National Geographic short turns the London Underground into a systems topic. Students can listen for engineering details, compare underground and surface transport, and discuss why old infrastructure needs constant adaptation in a modern city.

title: New York - Immigrants at Ellis Island
speaker: HISTORY
description: Learn why Ellis Island became a symbol of arrival, hope, inspection, and anxiety.
summary: This HISTORY short explains Ellis Island as a major immigration gateway in New York Harbor. Students can listen for numbers, procedures, emotions, and symbols, then discuss why a place of inspection could also become a place of hope and family memory.

title: New York - Building the Subway
speaker: Stuart Math
description: Use early subway construction to discuss speed, electricity, and city growth.
summary: This short history of New York subway construction introduces students to promises of speed, electric transport, tunnels, and the relationship between infrastructure and city growth. Students can compare early subway ambitions with modern complaints about transit reliability.

title: New York - The Street Vendors of the City
speaker: Street Vendor Project
description: Hear vendors explain work, flavor, permits, and belonging on city sidewalks.
summary: This short documentary presents New York street vendors as workers and community members, not just background city scenery. Students can identify arguments about permits, opportunity, food, and fairness, then compare street vending with markets or food stalls in other cities.

title: Cairo - Ancient Egypt in Six Minutes
speaker: National Geographic
description: Use a NatGeo overview to connect pyramids, pharaohs, religion, writing, and empire.
summary: This National Geographic overview gives students a compact introduction to ancient Egyptian civilization. It covers long timelines, powerful rulers, monuments, writing, religion, and cultural legacy. Students can separate ancient history from modern Cairo and discuss why ancient symbols still shape how many visitors imagine Egypt.

title: Dubai - Building Metro Connections

summary: This Roads and Transport Authority video connects the Dubai Metro to ambition, Expo-era planning, and the belief that rail can shape a future city. Students can compare metro investment with highways, taxis, and airport links, then discuss what public transport must do in extreme heat.

title: Dubai - From Creek Town to Global City
speaker: Around the world in under 10 minutes
description: Trace how trade, oil, ports, airlines, tourism, and finance reshaped Dubai.
summary: This short history overview gives students a compressed explanation of Dubai's growth from a trading settlement to a global city. It supports discussion about ports, oil revenue, aviation, tourism, finance, real estate, and city branding.

title: Sydney - What Lies Beneath the Harbour
speaker: ABC News Australia
description: Use an ABC News short to discuss hidden marine life below a famous view.
summary: This ABC News segment asks what people really know about life beneath Sydney Harbour. Students can contrast famous surface views with hidden ecosystems, discuss how cities affect water environments, and practice describing nature inside an urban setting.

title: Sydney - The Tumultuous Opera House Story
speaker: BBC Global
description: Learn why a famous building can be controversial before it becomes beloved.
summary: This BBC Global short explains the difficult history behind the Sydney Opera House. Students can discuss why ambitious architecture can create conflict, how public opinion changes over time, and what makes a building become a symbol of a city.

title: Sydney - How It Became Australia's Biggest City
speaker: Australia Reality TV
description: Trace geography, harbour access, migration, and growth in a compact city story.
summary: This short overview focuses on Sydney's rise as Australia's largest city. Students can identify the role of the harbour, migration, economy, and global image, then compare Sydney with capitals or port cities in other countries.

title: Beijing - A Capital in Two Minutes
speaker: The Millenium Studios
description: Trace how Beijing grew into a political and cultural capital.
summary: This short city history gives students a compact timeline for Beijing. They can identify dynasties, capital-city functions, and modern growth, then compare Beijing with other political capitals on the route.

title: Beijing - Life Inside the Hutongs
speaker: NeuLingo Chinese Learning
description: Use hutong neighborhoods to discuss memory, housing, tourism, and change.
summary: This culture video introduces Beijing hutongs as more than narrow lanes. Students can discuss family life, public space, preservation, and what is lost or gained when historic neighborhoods become tourist destinations.

title: Beijing - A Five-Star Subway Ride
speaker: CGTN
description: Look at how a huge city uses rail to make daily movement possible.
summary: This CGTN segment follows a foreign visitor exploring Beijing's subway. Students can notice ticketing, signs, scale, cleanliness, and passenger flow, then compare it with transit systems in other cities.

title: Shanghai - Towers, Temples, and Food
speaker: John & Sammy Iredale
description: Use a short city visit to notice skyline, old streets, temple space, and local eating.
summary: This compact visit moves through Shanghai skyline views, temple streets, and food experiences. It gives younger learners a concrete first look at the city without adding another transport lesson.

title: Shanghai - Food, Love, and Culture Shock
speaker: TEDx Talks
description: Hear a youth perspective on food, belonging, and cultural adjustment in Shanghai.
summary: This TEDx youth talk uses food and personal experience to discuss cultural adjustment. It supports class discussion about belonging, assumptions, and how ordinary meals can carry meaning.

title: Shanghai - Journey to the West in Five Minutes
speaker: RAS Shanghai
description: Use a classic Chinese story to explore literature, characters, and cultural memory.
summary: This short talk introduces Journey to the West through a Shanghai cultural institution. It gives advanced learners a culture-focused option about story, character, translation, and shared memory.

title: Berlin - The Wall Explained
speaker: explainitychannel
description: Understand why a wall divided a city and why its fall still matters.
summary: This explainer introduces the Berlin Wall as a political border inside everyday city life. Students can discuss division, movement, family separation, and why physical barriers can become powerful symbols.

title: Berlin - How to Use the Transport Network
speaker: Berlin
description: Use Berlin transit to practice routes, tickets, transfers, and city movement.
summary: This visitBerlin video explains public transport basics. Students can practice giving directions, comparing tickets, and describing why reliable transit changes how residents and visitors experience a city.

title: Berlin - The Blockade in Sixty Seconds
speaker: Drawn in 60 Seconds
description: Use a short history clip to discuss supply, pressure, and resilience.
summary: This compact animation introduces the Berlin Blockade. Students can identify the problem, the actors, and the response, then discuss why air routes mattered when roads and rail were blocked.

title: Moscow - A Concise City History
speaker: k.c.
description: Trace Moscow from settlement to capital and global city.
summary: This concise history clip gives students a city-specific timeline for Moscow. They can identify growth, political power, and rebuilding, then compare Moscow with other capitals in Europe and Asia.

title: Moscow - The Metro as a Public Palace
speaker: BBC
description: Explore why a subway can be transport, art, and state image at once.
summary: This BBC segment introduces the Moscow Metro as one of the world's busiest and most ornate systems. Students can discuss why stations might be decorated like palaces and how public transport can communicate pride.

title: Moscow - Kremlin and Red Square
speaker: UNESCO
description: Use a UNESCO clip to examine landmarks, symbolism, and public space.
summary: This UNESCO/NHK clip presents the Kremlin and Red Square as a World Heritage site. Students can practice describing landmarks while also asking why some places become symbols of national power.

title: Istanbul - When Constantinople Became Istanbul
speaker: History Matters
description: Use a short history video to discuss names, empire, and memory.
summary: This History Matters video explains the shift from Constantinople to Istanbul. Students can discuss how names carry memory, conquest, language, and identity, then compare cities with changed names in other countries.

title: Istanbul - Hagia Sophia to Suleymaniye
speaker: BBC
description: Compare religious buildings, architecture, and changing city identity.
summary: This BBC clip links Hagia Sophia and Suleymaniye Mosque to Istanbul's layered history. Students can compare form, function, and symbolism while practicing respectful language around religious heritage.

title: Istanbul - A City of Two Continents
speaker: Watch in 5ive
description: Use geography to explain movement, trade, ferries, and identity.
summary: This city overview focuses on Istanbul as a place between continents. Students can discuss bridges, boats, neighborhoods, and the Bosphorus as both a route and a symbol.

title: Vancouver - The Streams Hidden Under the City
speaker: CBC British Columbia
description: Investigate what happened to Vancouver streams as roads and neighborhoods developed.
summary: This CBC short film investigates the streams that once crossed Vancouver and asks what happened when many were buried beneath the growing city. Students can connect maps, urban development, salmon habitat, flooding, and restoration while evaluating whether hidden waterways should be brought back.

title: Vancouver - Riding the SkyTrain
speaker: Alexander College
description: Learn how an elevated rail system connects airport, suburbs, and downtown.
summary: This practical SkyTrain guide helps students practice transport language: stations, cards, transfers, routes, and arrival. It also opens discussion about why airport links matter for a global city.

title: Vancouver - A City in Nature
speaker: Destination Vancouver
description: Look at how parks, trees, mountains, and water shape a city identity.
summary: This Destination Vancouver short frames the city through nature. Students can compare Vancouver with cities where nature is distant, hidden, or built into everyday streets and views.

title: Toronto - Canada's Biggest City
speaker: Travis Ridgen 2.0
description: Explain how Toronto became a major Canadian and global city.
summary: This explainer focuses on Toronto's growth into Canada's largest city. Students can identify immigration, finance, geography, and regional connections, then compare Toronto with other national hubs.

title: Toronto - Public Transit Basics
speaker: theglobalcityproject
description: Use Toronto transit to discuss route planning, transfers, and urban scale.
summary: This short overview introduces public transit in Toronto. Students can practice giving route advice and discuss how transit shapes access to school, work, sports, and neighborhoods.

title: Toronto - World Cup Loyalties in a Multicultural City
speaker: Al Jazeera English
description: Discuss identity, immigration, sport, and belonging through soccer fandom.
summary: This Al Jazeera segment uses World Cup loyalties to show Toronto's multicultural identity. Students can discuss family roots, national teams, flags, and how sport can reveal layered belonging.

title: Mumbai - From Bombay to Mumbai
